newsitem.title: USA: Boeing says jumbo jet in crash was 14 years old.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says jumbo jet in crash was 14 years old.

text.p: The passenger jet destroyed in a midair collision with a cargo plane in India on Tuesday was a 14-year old Boeing 747-100, a spokesman for the manufacturer said.
The jumbo jet was delivered to Saudi Arabia's flag carrier March 17, 1982, and had logged nearly 15,000 flights and 40,000 hours, about average for a plane that age, said Boeing spokesman Doug Webb.
He did not immediately have any further information about the jet's service history.

Officials feared all 350 people aboard both planes were dead after the Saudi Arabian Airlines jet collided with a Kazakk Airlines Ilyushi IL-76 cargo jet more than two miles (four km) up in the air and 50 miles (80 km) outside New Delhi.

The 747-100 was the initial version of the jumbo jet that went into commercial service in 1970 and was produced by Boeing until 1986. A similar TWA 747-100 that exploded and crashed after taking off from New York in July was one of the oldest in service, having been delivered in 1971.
